{"data":{"id":"476754640949","type":"page","title":"Max Amount of Running Searches Error","status":"current","spaceId":"4708335613","snapshotToken":"v:2","detail":"full","body":{"format":"markdown","value":"**Max Amount of Running Searches Error – Secure 5**


When a user is running a search and gets an error indicating they have reached their max amount of running searches, it may need support intervention.



The error instructs the user should wait for one to complete or cancel other searches before trying again. However, if the situation is due to a server issue and not the user running too many searches, the suggestions in the error will not help.  Occasionally, if there is work being done on a server, such as a reboot or patching, it could leave queries in a pending status that will need to be manually cleared.


The issue could affect users from a single user at a single client to many users or multiple clients.


The first thing you will need to do is check the ‘secure.AsyncSearch’ table to see if there are in fact searches stuck in a pending status.


Before you can access the Before you can access the secure.AnySearch table, you first need to make sure you activate ‘My roles’ for PIM.

Once you have activated your PIM, then you need to RDP to the jump server.

Select your server and connect.  Then connect to the desired Client database.

 Once you have selected the Client database you will run the following search.  Make sure the ‘FROM’ address is for the correct Client. You will need to change it to use the search below.  We will run this search to see if searches are stuck in ‘Pending’.  


SELECT TOP (1000) \*

--update a set a.status = 5  
  FROM \[sqldb-prd-wus2-arp-production-138-nor-platform\].\[secure\].\[AsyncSearch\] a (nolock)  
  where status = 1 and StartDateTime \< DATEADD(HOUR, -1, CURRENT\_TIMESTAMP)  
  AND EndDateTime is null;


In the results above, there are a few things to note.  The ‘Status’ for all of them are ‘1’, the ‘EndDateTime’ is Null, and all the pending searches were on the same date, indicating something may have happened to Hatr to leave them in a bad state, especially if the data is several days in the past. 

These are the potential AsyncSearchStatus results.

Once you have run your first search and determined there is an issue with pending searches, you will run the update script that will change the status from Pending to ‘Cancelled’.  Again, make sure the ‘FROM’ address is for the correct Client. 


SELECT TOP (1000) \*

update a set a.status = 5  
  FROM \[sqldb-prd-wus2-arp-production-138-nor-platform\].\[secure\].\[AsyncSearch\] a (nolock)  
  where status = 1 and StartDateTime \< DATEADD(HOUR, -1, CURRENT\_TIMESTAMP)  
  AND EndDateTime is null;


This will return a message of the number of rows update, which should match the number of rows that came back on your first search.  The issue should now be resolved for the Clients.

You can run your first search again if you want to verify your search comes back empty.
